title: Arkret Principal Service Binding
description: Portable accepted-at binding between a principal and the Principal Server that hosted it, plus a bounded three-party-signed cutover chain to the current transport source.

accepted_at_service_binding_core.description: Frozen accepted-at binding core returned by ak.self.principal_service_binding.command.prepare. binding_digest = H('ak.principal-service-binding.v1', the RFC 8785 canonical object formed by every property here except binding_digest). authorization_challenge is service-generated, single-use and therefore binds the principal proof to this exact prepare instead of permitting an old proof to complete a later challenge. authority_evidence.document_digest MUST equal document_digest. A first binding omits predecessor_binding_digest and is accepted only when no current binding exists; a same-service renewal requires predecessor_binding_digest to equal the complete current binding digest under an atomic CAS.

endpoint_origins.description: Canonical HTTPS origins sorted by unsigned UTF-8 bytes. Paths, queries and fragments are forbidden by semantic validation.

service_resolution.description: First-hop route material for service_id. An inline record MUST name the same service_id; a referenced record MUST be fetched and independently verified before endpoint use.

authorization_challenge.description: Opaque service-generated challenge copied from the durable prepare record and included in binding_digest. It is never caller-selected or reused across distinct binding drafts.

predecessor_binding_digest.description: Exact current accepted binding digest replaced by this same-service renewal. Omitted only for the first accepted binding.

accepted_at_service_binding.description: Closed accepted-at snapshot installed by the two-phase self binding operation. principal_authorization_proof signs H('ak.principal-service-binding-proof.v1', {binding_digest,accepted_at,proof_purpose:'principal_authorization',verification_method,audience:service_id}); service_acceptance_proof signs the same closed object with proof_purpose='service_acceptance' and service_verification_method.id. Both signatures use the exact frozen core, fixed UTC-millisecond accepted_at and distinct proof purposes; neither proof enters binding_digest.

principal_service_cutover.description: One cutover edge. All three proofs sign H('ak.principal-service-cutover.v1', this object without principal_proof, previous_service_proof and new_service_proof). The principal proof prevents two services from transferring a principal between themselves; the old-service proof closes the prior writer fence; the new-service proof accepts the new binding. new_binding.principal_id and trust_domain MUST match the edge, new_binding.service_id MUST equal new_service_id, and new_binding.accepted_at MUST equal effective_at.

principal_service_binding_continuity.description: Accepted-at binding followed by zero or more cutovers. Edges are in ascending cutover_sequence, the first previous_binding_digest equals accepted_binding.binding_digest, every later edge links to the preceding new_binding, service_id values MUST NOT repeat, and the final binding service_id MUST equal the authenticated transport Source-Service-ID. An empty cutovers array requires accepted_binding.service_id to equal Source-Service-ID.
